text:
IncidentBot: Pager triggered — SLO alert: hosted-api redwood-prod-eu-1 TLS handshake failure rate ~35% over 5m, error spike at 18:13 UTC. Severity: P1. Auto-page: @maya (oncall).
maya: acked. I'm on it — joining call in 2m. Can someone grab customer impact and any regional trends?
cust-success-bot: customers impacted: approx 12 active API keys saw increased 5xx and TLS handshake failures. Top 3: acme-inc, dataplug, voxapps (partial degradations, retries spike). Notifying AMs.
liam: looking at edge LB metrics now. TLS failures concentrated in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. US regions normal. Curious if this lines up with last night's cert rotation job.
sasha: posting initial logs from the ingress LB. Note: redacted IPs.
```text
2026-03-14T18:11:02Z ERROR ssl_handshake: handshake failed: alert handshake failure (client hello) src=10.12.34.56 dst=34.56.78.90 sni="api.redwood.example.com"
2026-03-14T18:11:03Z ERROR ssl_handshake: cert presented: arn:aws:acm:...:cert/old-cert-2025
2026-03-14T18:11:04Z WARN  retry_logic: backend connection closed during handshake
```
maya: hmm that cert ARN looks like the pre-rotation artifact. @erika can you check cert rotation job / config? We rolled a new cert last night.
erika: checking cert-rotation job in k8s and ACM mappings. The rotation job finished at 03:07 UTC, but there was a follow-up patch to LB binding at 03:20 that shows partial failure on the NLB target group for eu clusters. Investigating logs now.
jonah: running quick TLS probe from vpc in eu-west-1:

```bash
# from bastion
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -servername api_redwood.example.com -showcerts
```

Output:

```text
CONNECTED(00000003)
139760... error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert internal error
---
no peer certificate
---
```
liam: interesting — s_client didn't even present cert details, we get an alert. Could be MTU/fragmentation during TLS handshake (ClientHello > MTU causing handshake errors) OR wrong cert binding causing immediate abort. Are we seeing any fragmentation or ICMP blackhole logs in VPC peering?
sasha: I pulled tcpdump from the front-line proxy (small capture) — see snippet. Note many SYN+ACK followed by no further packets, and several TCP retransmits before the connection resets.
```text
18:10:58.123 IP client -> lb: Flags [S], seq 0...
18:10:58.124 IP lb -> client: Flags [S.], seq 0...
18:11:00.500 IP client -> lb: Flags [P.], seq ... (ClientHello)
18:11:03.700 IP lb -> client: Flags [R], seq ... (RST)
```
erika: checked VPC peering config between infra-vpc and edge-network: peering active, but I see an MTU mismatch — infra-vpc has mtu 9001, edge-network was set to 1500 after an overlay change last week. That could cause packet fragmentation issues for larger ClientHello messages with many extensions/cert chains.
maya: good catch. That would cause sporadic handshake failures, especially for clients sending large TLS SNI/ALPN lists or when we serve long cert chains. What's the distribution of failed handshakes vs cipher suites / client hello size?
liam: pulling LB logs that include client_hello_length. Quick summary: failures correlate with client_hello sizes > 1400 bytes. Also, cert chain size got larger after we added new intermediates in the rotation — chain length increased ~900 bytes. So combined ClientHello + cert size pushing packets past MTU.
jonah: can reproduce locally by forcing small MTU on a test interface. When MTU is small and DF is set, we see exactly the same behavior: ClientHello gets dropped or handshake aborts. Repro steps:

```bash
ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400
curl -v --tlsv1.3 https://api.redwood.example.com
# observe: SSL handshake error, no cert presented
```

maya: mitigation plan suggestions?
liam: short-term: route traffic away from affected eu clusters to healthy regions (automatic failover) and enable TCP MSS clamping on peering gateways so large packets are lowered to fit MTU. Also rollback the LB cert binding to previous cert that produced smaller chain? That feels risky.
sasha: we can push MSS clamping on the edge-router quickly — config change staged, ready to apply in 2m. That should reduce fragmentation and likely bring handshake success rates up.
erika: on cert rotation: the rotation job did add one intermediate which increased overall chain size. The LB binding script attempted to update NLB listener certs, but AWS API returned partial success for some target ARNs due to a race. So some LBs have old certs and some have new chains. That mismatch + MTU causes unpredictable behavior.
maya: okay action items for now:
- enable MSS clamping on edge-router for eu peering (sasha)
- adjust route policy to shift ~30% of traffic to us-east-1 as fallback (liam)
- verify cert binding consistency across all NLBs and rollback if mismatch found (erika)
- notify customers about partial degraded access and retries recommended (cust-success-bot)

sasha: MSS clamping applied at 18:28 UTC. Monitoring handshake metric now.

```text
18:29:00 TLS handshake failures: 35% -> 8% (steady)
18:31:00 TLS handshake failures: 8% -> 2% -> stabilizing ~1.5%
```

maya: nice. liam can you start a gradual traffic shift to healthy regions and monitor error rates and latency? We'll keep some traffic on eu until certs are stable.

liam: starting traffic shift at 18:35 UTC. Moving 15% every 2 minutes. Observability: error rate drops in region as expected.
erika: cert binding audit: found 4 NLB listeners still referencing arn:old-cert-2025. Applied binding update to those listeners at 18:40 UTC and forced cert refresh. After refresh, chain length remains larger but MSS clamping handles fragmentation. Double-checking ACM shows rotation completed and no expirations.
jonah: running end-to-end tests from clients with various TLS stacks. All tests pass after MSS clamp + cert binding updates. Some older clients (legacy cipher sets) still show intermittent issues — might be unrelated but logging.
maya: customer impact update: handshake failures reduced from 35% -> 1.5% within 20 minutes of mitigation. No ongoing data loss; retries recovered most requests. AMs pinged with status that service is degraded and then recovered; follow-up RCA and postmortem to be created.
liam: hypothesis tracker (in-thread):
- Hypothesis A: MTU mismatch causing fragmentation + large ClientHello -> OBSERVABLE -> Supported by tcpdump + client_hello_size correlation -> Mitigation effective (MSS clamp) -> Marked probable.
- Hypothesis B: Partial cert binding (mix of old/new certs) creating inconsistent chain lengths and negotiation differences -> OBSERVABLE -> Found mismatched NLB bindings -> Mitigation performed (binding update) -> Marked probable.
- Hypothesis C: Cipher mismatch or application bug -> NOT SUPPORTED by evidence (ciphers mostly OK), keep monitoring for legacy clients.
sasha: capturing final logs for RCA. Will store full tcpdumps and LB logs to the incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/2026-03-14/1719998427/
erika: root cause summary draft: during scheduled cert rotation we introduced an extra intermediate cert increasing chain size; concurrently a configuration drift changed MTU on edge-network to 1500 creating a mismatch with infra-vpc (9001). Large TLS handshakes began hitting fragmentation limits across peering, causing handshake failures. Partial NLB binding failures left mixed certs across regions exacerbating client negotiations. Combined, this created widespread TLS handshake failures. Mitigations: MSS clamping, cert binding reconciliation, traffic shift, and completed rotation.
maya: handing off to @liam for follow-up RCA and action items. I'm stepping off call at 19:05 UTC. Summary for handoff: mitigations applied, customer impact contained, logs archived, next steps are root cause writeup and automation to prevent mixed bindings.

liam: taking over. OOO: schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Initial action items I'm owning:
1) Automate cert binding verification after rotation (script + canary tests) — due 2026-03-21
2) Add MTU-monitoring alert for peering (detect mismatches) — due 2026-03-18
3) Document MSS-clamp as a runbook mitigation with exact router commands — due 2026-03-17
4) Retro: revisit rotation chain size limits and consider short cert chains or OCSP stapling options — due 2026-03-30

cust-success-bot: AMs notified, ticket #INC-2026-1847 created and linked.
maya: thanks all. Closing the active pager; keep thread updated if anything regresses. We'll include timeline, logs, and final RCA in the postmortem doc.
